narrative: The tech world sees rapid advancements in AI, with new models and agentic capabilities from OpenAI, Google, and NVIDIA driving innovation in development, enterprise, and daily applications. Concurrently, discussions around AI safety, ethical use, and economic impact are intensifying, alongside significant developments in space exploration and cloud infrastructure.

highlights.title: Meet GPT-Red: an LLM super-hacker OpenAI built to make its models safer
highlights.whyItMatters: OpenAI is using an LLM super-hacker to improve the defenses of its other models against cyberattacks, emphasizing AI safety.

highlights.title: It's official: EU will force Google to share search data and open up AI on Android
highlights.whyItMatters: New EU regulations will mandate Google to share search data and open up AI on Android, raising user privacy and competition concerns.

highlights.title: NASA Pushes New Wing Design to Find Structural Limits
highlights.whyItMatters: NASA's successful testing of a novel wing design suggests significant advancements in lightweight aerospace structures.

highlights.title: Patreon stops asking AI bots not to scrape — and starts blocking them
highlights.whyItMatters: Patreon is taking active measures to block AI bots from scraping content, emphasizing creator rights and data protection.

highlights.title: Accelerate your infrastructure deployments by up to 4x with AWS CloudFormation Express mode
highlights.whyItMatters: AWS CloudFormation's new Express mode significantly boosts infrastructure deployment speed, benefiting AI agents and developers.

highlights.title: Google is open-sourcing its 3D emoji
highlights.whyItMatters: Google's decision to open-source its 3D emoji allows wider creative use and highlights trends in accessible digital assets.

highlights.title: ChatGPT is now a partner for your most ambitious work
highlights.whyItMatters: OpenAI's ChatGPT Work can now act as an agent for complex projects, enhancing productivity across various tasks and applications.
